old_implementation_control.adaptation: The same probe calls legacy commit instead of try_commit, forces legacy buffered payload writeback by reading the root, then compares the entire file context after injected payload write failure.

probe_constraints: SWAP and the current disk-backed SXMS stub are tested with optional cache allocations refused during fixture setup.
The target fixed index record crosses a 16 KiB page boundary; both first-write and later-write refusal are injected.
Root payload reads evict append-tail replacement data before injecting read failures. Reading the last fixture does not guarantee eviction.
Each failed commit compares the complete TFileContext before any successful retry; text, links, line number, aliases, cursor, and selection are also checked explicitly.
Command fault cases invoke Save, Save As, Save All, Close, and Exit with current-document payload write refusal. A BIOS hook acknowledges the error dialog.
Pending index rollback blocks further replacement payload writes. Close refusal keeps the payload owner, deletion refusal retains cleanup state, and discard retry releases owned heap.
Dirty payload discard is tested while writes are refused and must issue no payload writes.
DOS-store growth allocation refusal preserves the file context and line links; retry after heap release updates relocated aliases.
Old and orphaned payloads remain allocated until store discard. This is runtime replacement safety, not crash recovery or qualified long-session disk usage.
Legacy editing commit/put callers outside the save/close/exit paths remain unchecked.
remaining: Migrate remaining editor commit/put callers and propagate failures through full commands
Safe old/orphaned payload reclamation and checked free-list mutation
Checked loading, navigation, rendering, and multi-record editing
Full-command low-memory and final runtime qualification
